History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female presents with 3-day history of dysuria, mild hematuria, and lower abdominal discomfort; clinical impression is an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) and empiric oral antibiotics were prescribed.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Pain (“stinging”) on micturition for the past 3 days.  
• Course/progression: Persistent; neither improving nor worsening.  
• Lower abdominal pain: Mild, cramp-like, concurrent with voiding; does not radiate to back or flanks.  
• Hematuria: Small amount noted earlier today.  
• Urine odor: Described as “smells a bit weird.”  
• Urinary frequency/urgency: Denies increased frequency; no urgency reported.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, flank pain, back pain.  
• Bowel function: Normal; no diarrhea.  
• Gynecologic history: Last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago; denies abnormal vaginal discharge. Sexually active with new partner (2 months); uses condoms. No prior sexually transmitted infection screening.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No vaginal discharge, no flank pain, no systemic symptoms (fever, rigors), no gastrointestinal upset beyond baseline IBS.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) – no current medications, no recent flares mentioned.  
• No history of kidney or bladder disease noted.

Medications:
• No regular prescription medications.  
• Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate “a couple of days ago” for pain – not effective.  
(All other medication history not documented.)

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – causes swelling (likely angioedema) – severe; avoid.

Social History:
• Lives in an off-campus flat with friends; college biology student.  
• Smoking: Denies tobacco use.  
• Alcohol: Social drinking on weekends.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  
• Sexual activity: Sexually active with one male partner (condom use).  
• Occupation: Full-time student; no employment noted.

Family History:
• No known family history of renal, bladder, or gastrointestinal diseases.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person exam performed during telehealth visit; no vitals provided.)

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Dysuria / probable uncomplicated urinary tract infection  
  • Assessment: 3-day history of dysuria, mild hematuria, malodorous urine, and lower abdominal discomfort without systemic symptoms → consistent with simple cystitis.  
  • Plan:  
    – Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin OR Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact drug/dose/route not documented).  
    – Hydration: Encourage high oral fluid intake; consider cranberry juice.  
    – Symptom monitoring: Educate on red-flag symptoms (fever, flank/back pain, worsening condition).  
    – Follow-up: If no improvement by end of week or if red-flag symptoms develop, call or return for reassessment.  
    – Sexual activity: Advise abstaining until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  

Issue 2: Pregnancy possibility  
  • Assessment: Low likelihood but not excluded.  
  • Plan: Advised patient to perform a pregnancy test if any concern or if symptoms persist.

Issue 3: STI screening / sexual health  
  • Assessment: Sexually active with new partner, never screened.  
  • Plan: Recommended routine STI screening at appropriate clinic (not arranged during call).

General plan items:  
• Allergy documented; avoid Clindamycin.  
• Provide written or electronic safety-netting instructions.  

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: Vitals, physical examination findings, urine dip/culture, medication reconciliation beyond OTC bicarbonate, detailed antibiotic name/dose/route.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal irrelevant dialogue; telehealth format limited physical exam data.
